review: P4 native code-generation comparison before the isolated I2C0 Box candidate
method: Read-only static examination of the already compiled baseline and candidate ELF files; no builds, executable runs, performance samples, or Rust edits were performed for this review.

candidate.sourceCommitFormat: full Git commit resolved from the frozen candidate revision 91d7975

architecture: ELF 64-bit LSB PIE, x86-64, with debug information, not stripped
tools: Python 3 standard library (subprocess, re, difflib, collections, hashlib, json)

normalization.symbolSelection: Match full demangled function names using nm -S --demangle; obtain address and size from the matching symbol.
normalization.disassembly: Disassemble from the exact symbol start to start+size with objdump -d --demangle --no-show-raw-insn.
normalization.instructionCounts: Count instruction lines with a hexadecimal address followed by a colon; counts include alignment instructions and cold panic paths and are static function counts, not dynamic executed instruction counts.
normalization.addresses: Remove each instruction address; replace branch/call absolute target addresses with their displayed demangled symbol and relative offset. Normalize RIP-relative displacement values while retaining the referenced symbol annotation.
normalization.whitespace: Collapse runs of whitespace to a single space.
normalization.fieldComparison: For the five equal-length functions below, compare corresponding normalized instruction lines. Classify a line as a displacement-only change only when all non-displacement instruction text matches; retain and subtract old/new hexadecimal memory displacements explicitly.
normalization.additionalDifferenceHandling: Report address-arithmetic immediates and relocated diagnostic/data constant annotations separately. Do not remove arbitrary constants or register-allocation differences to claim equivalence.
normalization.scope: Function-level native code shapes and explicit memory operands; this is not a complete binary-equivalence proof.

functions.calls: Both versions call the independent Peripherals::source_status function; no newly outlined call.

otherDifferences: One relocated panic diagnostic constant annotation.
functions.calls: Same call sequence in both versions: tick_optional, TimerGroup::tick, I2c::tick, TimerGroup::tick, Ledc::tick, panic_bounds_check.

otherDifferences: One address-arithmetic instruction changes add $0x1ba0,%rdx to add $0x1c58,%rdx (+184).
Six relocated diagnostic/data constant annotations; RIP-relative library entry addresses were normalized.
functions.calls: Same direct and indirect call sequence in both versions, including the independent Peripherals::tick calls.

sourceStatus.inlining: Independent symbol and an explicit call from refresh_irq exist in both binaries; no newly introduced loss of inlining was observed.
sourceStatus.sourceChange: The new optional I2C0 source 44 adds bit 12 to optional source word 1; the previous optional USB_OTG source 93 occupies word 2.
sourceStatus.finding: The candidate merges cached words 1 and 2 together using SIMD. The rest of the source aggregation also changes register allocation and branch/arithmetic shape; the whole function is smaller despite adding an IRQ source.
sourceStatus.frequencyContext: The unchanged P4 Bus::tick returns 1, so Machine::after_round invokes refresh_irq each scheduling round, independently of whether I2C0 is active.
sourceStatus.warning: Do not equate the extra tail logic with a fixed net dynamic instruction increase for the complete function.

preAccess.inlining: Independent function symbols exist in both binaries.
preAccess.finding: The candidate saves/restores one additional register and copies the self pointer at function entry. New GPIO-routing calls remain inside the I2C0 address/configuration branch; no per-tick GPIO route parsing was added.

recommendation.firstCandidate: Change only the P4 i2c0 field from I2c to Box<I2c>, and wrap its constructor in Box::new.
recommendation.reason: The already compiled binaries demonstrate a widespread +184-byte shift in old hot fields while retaining the relevant hot call structures. A local allocation change directly addresses this observed difference.
recommendation.inliningAssessment: The existing inline always option would introduce a new code-generation policy; no regression from newly outlined source_status/tick calls was observed to justify trying it first.
recommendation.preservation: Keep independent I2C0/I2C1 clocks, MMIO routing, optional activation, deadline delivery and pending IRQ behavior unchanged.

priorMechanisms.relevance: Prior native codegen evidence distinguishes newly cached optional IRQ words from layout changes; adding even a Box pointer can shift pre-existing fields.
Idle-layout/code-shape effects require measured validation; source-level coldness alone does not establish zero cost.
Optional I2C deadlines and stopped-controller pending IRQs must retain their existing semantics.

limits: The completed original performance receipt is separate and was not modified or resampled by this review.
No static codegen observation proves that field movement or IRQ aggregation caused all or any specific fraction of the measured CPU regression.
Static instruction counts are not dynamic work, elapsed time, host instructions retired, cache misses, or branch mispredictions.
Box<I2c> can still change enclosing layouts by a pointer-sized amount; it is not claimed to restore all baseline offsets or performance before measurement.
Only the listed functions and relevant source paths were examined; this is not a complete native, WASM, firmware, or hardware correctness review.
Do not skip optional IRQ cache aggregation solely because active_optional is empty: a completed I2C controller can be idle while its completion interrupt remains asserted.
The proposed two-line candidate had not been built or measured when these findings were recorded.
